name: Jahdiel
title: Head of the half-tribe of Manasseh
summary: Jahdiel was one of the heads of the eastern half of the tribe of Manasseh. He is mentioned in 1 Chronicles as a brave warrior and a well-known family leader among his people. He belonged to the tribes that were later led into exile by the king of Assyria because of unfaithfulness to God.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned as a family head in the tribe of Manasseh
keyEvents.description: Jahdiel is listed as one of the family heads in the eastern half of the tribe of Manasseh, known as a brave warrior.

keyEvents.title: Described as brave warriors
keyEvents.description: Jahdiel and the other tribal leaders are described as brave warriors and famous men, heads of their families.

keyEvents.title: The tribe's unfaithfulness to God
keyEvents.description: The eastern half of the tribe of Manasseh, including Jahdiel's people, were unfaithful to the God of their fathers and practiced idolatry with the peoples of the land.

keyEvents.title: Assyria's exile of the eastern tribes
keyEvents.description: As a result of the tribe's unfaithfulness, God allowed the Assyrian king Tiglath-Pileser to lead them into exile, including the half-tribe of Manasseh.
